narrative:
The 2017 San Diego Padres entered the season as a rebuilding club, and the results largely confirmed that reality — a 71-91 record and a run differential of minus-212 left no illusions about where this franchise stood. Yet within that losing season were genuine flashes of excitement, particularly from an offense that muscled up for 189 home runs and a handful of youngsters who gave the fanbase reasons to believe better days were coming.

April was a rough introduction to the year, but not without its moments. Austin Hedges delivered a stunning two-run blast and Ryan Schimpf launched a go-ahead three-run shot that thrilled Petco Park. The problem was the bullpen, where Brandon Maurer repeatedly squandered leads, becoming the season's most consistent villain. His name appeared on one damaging play after another — single after single, home run surrendered — as the Padres went 11-16 in May and struggled to stay competitive against better opponents.

June brought more of the same inconsistency, but July was the Padres' one genuine bright spot, posting a 14-11 record that teased a different kind of team. Yangervis Solarte was a steady offensive presence, and the rotation showed enough fight to win close games. Sadly, August and September represented the season's extended collapse, as the bullpen — Brad Hand, Kirby Yates, and others — gave away winnable games with agonizing regularity. Grand slams, walk-off homers, and late-inning implosions became a recurring theme.

The season closed with a few individual highlights — Carlos Asuaje's clutch bases-clearing single in September and Austin Hedges' go-ahead double in the penultimate game stood out as reminders of the talent quietly developing in San Diego. But the final record told the true story: a franchise still searching for its identity, collecting useful pieces like Hedges, Hunter Renfroe, and Manuel Margot, and hoping that a more disciplined roster-building approach would eventually turn promise into contention.

chapters.title: Early Sparks, Early Stumbles
chapters.description: The Padres open the year with some electrifying home runs but the bullpen — led by Brandon Maurer's meltdowns — ensures a losing April.

chapters.title: Grinding Through May and June
chapters.description: San Diego battles through a difficult two-month stretch with the offense providing occasional fireworks but the pitching staff giving too much back.

chapters.title: July Surge
chapters.description: The Padres post their best month of the season at 14-11, with Yangervis Solarte leading the charge and the team showing genuine competitive fight.

chapters.title: August Unraveling
chapters.description: The bullpen falls apart in August as Brad Hand, Kirby Yates, and others surrender crushing home runs that turn winnable games into losses.

chapters.title: September Glimmers
chapters.description: Young players like Carlos Asuaje and Austin Hedges deliver clutch moments down the stretch, offering a hopeful preview of the Padres' future even as the losing season winds down.
